content.title: Is Home Depot open on Easter?
content.text: Weekends are for home projects, and Easter weekend is no different than any other for plenty of Americans. Whether this Sunday includes yard work, closet organizing or other spring cleaning, Home Depot likely has many of the supplies you need to get the jobs done. So you’ll be happy to know that The Home Depot will be open for business on Sunday, April 5. According to the Home Depot website, stores will be open from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. Home Depot has seen a decline in foot traffic in recent years.Suhail/Getty Images · Suhail/Getty Images Home Depot is one of those stores that rarely closes. In fact, Home Depot only closes two days each year: Thanksgiving Day and Christmas Day. Home Depot, Inc. accounts for 52.4% of the home improvement market ($149.5 billion a year), according to data from IBISWorld. Still, visits to Home Depot have been down, so the company needs to keep its doors open as many days as possible. Home Depot's foot traffic declined about 3.8% year over year in Q1 2026, according to Placer.ai data shared on Yahoo Finance. Home Depot is open on Easter, which is good news if you're planning to tackle home projects. And even though the Home Depot website says stores are open on Easter, use the Home Depot locator to make sure your store is. Plenty of other major retailers are also open. Kroger is open normal hours, but pharmacies are closed. Harris Teeter stores are open normal hours. Meijer stores are open from 6 a.m. to midnight. Stop and Shop locations are open from 7 a.m. to 5 p.m., but pharmacies are closed. Trader Joe’s plans to be open regular business hours. Walmart is open normal hours. Whole Foods locations are open until 6 p.m. Winn-Dixie stores will be open normal business hours. Sources: Store websites Related: Home Depot sees worrisome shift in consumer behavior This story was originally published by TheStreet on Apr 5, 2026, where it first appeared in the Retail section. Add TheStreet as a Preferred Source by clicking here. Jack Nivison 5 April 2026 1 min read Aussies will be able to get supplies this Easter long weekend. Picture: NewsWire / Gaye Gerard The Easter long weekend is here, which means that a number of major outlets and grocery chains will be altering or reducing their hours during annual celebrations. Here is a comprehensive list of all the stores that are open and shut across the Easter weekend. Easter Monday Most major retailers will reopen on Easter Monday, after mass closures through parts of the long weekend. Woolworths, Coles and Aldi stores across the country will trade on Easter Monday at varied operating hours. Major supermarkets will trade on Easter Monday. Picture: NewsWire/ Gaye Gerard Stores will open at varied operating hours. Westfield shopping centres in the ACT will trade from 10am-4pm; those in Victoria will be open from 10am-5pm, and all NSW centres will be open at varying hours. Westfield centres will be closed in SA. Those in WA will trade from 11am-5pm. Bunnings stores will be open on Easter Monday, with residents encouraged to check their local store’s hours. Phoebe Griffiths 31 December 2025 2 min read The ultimate guide to what’s open on the first day of 2026. Picture: NewsWire / Flavio Brancaleone Major retailers have revealed their New Year’s Day trading hours for 2026, with South Australia facing the most widespread closures. Here is a guide to what’s open on Thursday, January 1. Woolworths Most stores will be open as normal with the exception of some stores in South Australia and Northern Territory that will be closed all day. Coles Coles stores be open everywhere with the exception of South Australia. Adelaide Rundle Place Coles is the only metropolitan Coles to open, trading from 11am--5pm. Regional South Australian stores will be open from 8am-8pm. Most Coles will be open as normal except in South Australia. Picture: NewsWire/ Gaye Gerard Liquorland If you are missing some supplies on January 1, Liquorland stores will be open as normal in most states. South Australians should check the opening hours of their local stores, with these stores closing on the day: Greenacres, Gawler Green, Firle, Elizabeth, Parafield Gardens, St Agnes, West Lakes, Paralowie, Port Adelaide, Modbury Heights, Churchill, Athelstone, Munno Para, St Clair, North Adelaide and McLaren Vale. Dan Murphy Dan Murphy stores will be open from 10am-7pm. BWS BWS stores will be open, with some stores affected by altered public holiday trading hours. Most liquor stores will be open for all of your New Year’s Day needs. Picture: NewsWire/ Gaye Gerard Westfield Westfield shopping centres will vary – some will be open with reduced hours, the ACT and South Australian stores will be closed and in NSW most stores will be closed too. Bunnings Bunnings trading hours will vary throughout the country, so it is best to check with your local store. Kmart, Big W and Target Most stores will be open but may trade under different hours. Opening hours are expected to resume back to normal on January 2. Picture: NewsWire / Flavio Brancaleone Fast food Most major fast-food chains will be ready to soothe hangovers on New Year’s Day – McDonald’s, KFC, Guzman y Gomez, Domino’s, Hungry Jack’s and Subway will all be open but possibly with reduced hours. Petrol stations and convenience stores Convenience stores such as 7-Eleven will be open as normal, along with most petrol stations. Andrew Hedgman 24 January 2026 4 min read Australia Day brings a long weekend and public holiday trading, but the rules change depending on where you live. Australians are set to enjoy a long weekend as Australia Day falls on Monday, giving many the perfect excuse to relax, catch up with friends, or head out and enjoy what’s on offer. Whether you’re planning a barbecue, tackling a home project, or squeezing in some shopping before the festivities, most major retailers and services will be open nationwide, although trading hours will vary depending on where you live. Major shopping centres follow state-specific trading rules: Canberra Centre and Canberra Outlet in the ACT will be open, while Rundle Mall in Adelaide will trade from 11am to 5pm. Picture: NewsWire / John Gass Supermarkets and major retailers Coles and Woolworths supermarkets will largely remain open across the country, with public holiday hours applying in most states. Stores in NSW, Victoria, the ACT and Tasmania are expected to trade close to normal hours, while Queensland outlets will generally open later and close earlier unless located in tourist precincts. South Australia will again have the strictest rules, with most metropolitan supermarkets closed and limited CBD and regional trading available. Western Australia and the Northern Territory will operate under government-approved public holiday hours. Big W and Kmart will also trade across most of the country, though several South Australian and regional stores will close for the day. DIY enthusiasts can breathe easy, with Bunnings Warehouse stores open nationwide throughout the long weekend. Trade Centres, however, will remain closed on the public holiday. Liquor stores Bottle shops will be open in most areas, making it easy to stock up for celebrations. Dan Murphy’s stores are expected to open from about 10am and close between 6pm and 7pm, while BWS and Liquorland outlets will trade with reduced hours depending on state and council regulations. Some regional and remote stores may remain closed. Bunnings Warehouse stores are open nationwide, so DIY enthusiasts can still tackle home projects, though Trade Centres will remain closed for the public holiday. Picture: NewsWire / Andrew Henshaw Shopping centres Shopping centre trading will depend heavily on state legislation. Centres in the ACT, parts of Queensland and the Northern Territory will be open with reduced hours, while South Australia’s Rundle Mall will be one of the few metropolitan shopping districts open in that state. Transport and services Public transport services will run on public holiday or weekend timetables in major cities, with additional services in some areas to support Australia Day events and fireworks. Commuters are advised to plan ahead, particularly in Sydney and Perth, where road closures and ferry disruptions will occur around evening celebrations. Australia Post outlets will be closed, with no mail deliveries taking place. Many cafes and restaurants will open but may apply a public holiday surcharge of about 10–15 per cent. Australia Day 2026: Key times and highlights by state Shoppers are advised to check local store hours before heading out, as trading times differ widely depending on state, council regulations, and location. Picture: NewsWire / John Appleyard NSW Supermarkets: Most Coles and Woolworths stores open with public holiday hours Updated 30 March 2026 3 min read Centrelink offices and call centres will be closed for the public holidays on Good Friday and Easter Monday. (Source: Getty) Millions of Centrelink recipients are being urged to plan ahead for the upcoming Easter holidays. All service centres and most call centres will be closed for the public holidays, which means you might need to report early if you still want to get paid on time. The closures on Good Friday and Easter Monday will impact most payments and allowances. That includes those receiving the Age Pension, JobSeeker, Youth Allowance, ABSTUDY and Austudy, Carer Allowance, Disability Support Pension, and Parenting Payment. “We want to help you plan so you still get paid. You may need to report your income early so we can pay you during these closures. We may pay you early,” Services Australia said. RELATED Centrelink recipients reminded to register for $475 million robodebt payout Aussie council backs down on four-day work week for employees in face of public 'hostility' Calls for Aussie venues to ditch controversial 'fun tax' in surcharge and wages debate Service centres, agents, access points and most call centres will close for the Easter public holidays. Those are Good Friday on April 3 and Easter Monday on April 6. While physical offices will be shut, people can still use their Centrelink online account or self-service options to report their income. But if you report on the public holidays, you will be paid after the public holidays. If the dates you normally report to Centrelink are impacted by the public holiday, you’ll need to report your income earlier on a new date. There have been changes to five normal reporting dates: Tuesday March 31, Wednesday April 1, Thursday April 2, Friday April 3, and Monday April 6. Your new reporting and payment dates will depend on your normal dates. Your Centrelink online account will show your new reporting date, or you can also see the specific changes here. If you report early, don’t forget you need to include what you expect to be paid for that entire reporting period. If you make a mistake, you can correct your report within 14 days, or when you next report. If you don’t have to report to get your payment, you may be paid early. This is your normal payment, just paid early. For example, if your normal payment date was on Easter Monday on April 6, your revised payment date would be Thursday, April 2. “When we make an early payment, we pay before your normal payment day and as close to it as possible. You’ll need to budget so this payment lasts until your next payment day,” Services Australia said. Cameron Micallef 3 April 2026 4 min read Businesses will have to pay up to 250 per cent more in staffing costs over the April long weekends. Picture: NewsWire / John Appleyard Australians will cop a collective $179m hit to their wallets due to holiday surcharges in April if they visit a cafe, pub or restaurant, but businesses say they are simply passing on skyrocketing costs. Penalty rates will lead to hospitality workers’ salaries jumping by as much as 250 per cent over the long weekend as compensation for working the public holiday. Australian Retail Credit Association chief executive Wes Lambert told NewsWire that even the best-run cafes and restaurants were still spending between 30 to 40 per cent of costs on staff on a typical trading day, with holidays leading to skyrocketing bills for businesses. “Now if you are paying up to 250 per cent of that number, 2.5 times 40 is 100. That means the moment a cafe or restaurant opens its doors on a weekend or public holiday they could be losing money,” he said. Businesses will have to pay up to 250 per cent more in staffing costs over the April long weekends. Picture: NewsWire / John Appleyard Mr Lambert says the high hospitality wage costs are similar to those in the car and recycling industries that eventually caused them to close. “You cannot squeeze blood out of a rock. Ultimately, if consumers and politicians want to dine and drink on the weekend or public holiday it is going to cost them more,” Mr Lambert said. “There are no other solutions, the only feasible way is for hospitality to close on the weekend and public holidays.” Mr Lambert said more Australian businesses were simply closing during the holiday period because prices were too high. “If wages continue to increase at the rate they have been increasing at the past few years, then we will likely be paying a barista $100 per hour on a public holiday by the time the Olympics arrives,” he said “We are already paying them nearly $70 an hour. It is unsustainable and nobody seems to see this brick wall we are racing towards.” Citing CreditorWatch figures, Mr Lambert said hospitality businesses were closing at double the rate of any other sector in the economy. “The average consumer does not want to pay more for coffee, pints, steaks or schnitties, and we are woefully underpriced for government-controlled parts of our businesses including wages and superannuation,” Mr Lambert said. Australians are set to spend an extra $179m over the public holidays. Picture: NewsWire / John Appleyard Record surcharges hit wallets hard As small businesses pass on rising costs to consumers, Aussie households face another financial gut punch over the long weekend. Research from financial comparison platform money.com.au prepared exclusively for NewsWire estimates Australians will spend a whopping $129.7m in surcharges over the Easter long weekend alone when dining out at restaurants, cafes and pubs. When the Anzac long weekend is added in, households are expected to be surcharged an additional $49.2m. Updated 4 March 2026 4 min read The cost of chocolate has been hard to swallow. But it should get cheaper in the second half of the year. (Source: Getty/Yahoo Finance) The cost of living is coming for the Easter Bunny this year. Shoppers in Coles and Woolworths have been taken aback by some of the hefty price tags on their usual festive favourites this year. Data shows some items are up by more than 30 per cent compared to the same time last year. The good news is that markets show price relief for chocolate treats is almost certainly on the way. But the bad news is it won't come in time for the Easter long weekend this year. The price of cocoa in the international commodities markets has been on a wild ride recently, but has now fallen dramatically from around US$12,000 per ton to just over US$3,000 per ton. "That would suggest you would expect probably at the back end of this year, and maybe next Easter in 2027, you'll see lower prices," Professor Gary Mortimer told Yahoo Finance. RELATED Families turn to camping holidays 'out of necessity' as caravan sharing platform booms Millions of Aussie workers could get extra week of annual leave under new union push Laid off Aussie workers chasing $40,000 payouts warned as 'embarrassing' claims spike Mortimer, a retail expert at Queensland University of Technology, said he went digging into the commodities markets recently looking for answers after seeing a lot of videos on social media of Aussie shoppers balking at the high prices of easter items on the shelves at Coles and Woolworths supermarkets. Shoppers have taken to social media to share their disbelief at some of the prices. But relief is in the pipeline. (Source: TikTok) Cocoa prices surged dramatically in 2024 due to a combination of severe weather, crop diseases and supply disruptions in West Africa – which sources about half of the world's cocoa supply, he explained. "But cocoa prices are falling on the back of softer demand. We are buying less because it's expensive," he said. Supply is also ramping up this year as weather conditions improve and new plantings in Ecuador reach maturity – all helping to see a price crash that should eventually flow through, at least in part, to the supermarket aisle. "What I would expect to see, hopefully, is that those lower cost prices being passed on to consumers late in the year and early next year," Mortimer said. "Not just Easter eggs, we're talking about any sort of chocolate product – chocolate ice cream, chocolate bars, things like that." He said most of the Easter products currently on display have been in store since "from sort of Boxing Day onwards" so it will take a while for the relief in commodities markets to translate into hip pocket relief for chocoholics. According to data from AI price comparison tool Zyft, Easter chocolates have increased by an average of 26.6 per cent year-on-year, with some favourites like the Crunchie Hollow Egg spiking by 33 per cent.
